A glowing volcanic forge-cavern, lava channels carved into the floor like veins, the dragon's collected weapons racked along the walls, everything lit by the deep orange pulse of a magma river running beneath an iron grate.

A drowned sea-palace, flooded throne-room of a sunken kingdom, broken columns trailing seaweed, a tilted coral-crusted throne, pale green light filtering down through fathoms of water far above the vaulted ceiling.

A frozen glacier ice-cave, walls of deep blue ice shot through with ancient cracks, a frozen longship and suspended armored knights visible within the translucent walls, cold diffused daylight glowing through the ceiling.
A treetop aerie atop a colossal ancient tree, a vast nest of timber, bone, ship-mast and gathered gold open to a wide sunset sky, the forest canopy rolling away in every direction below.

A claimed library-temple, soaring vaulted stone with shelves carved into every wall, shafts of amber and violet falling through shattered stained-glass windows onto the dragon's carefully arranged hoard of tomes and scrolls.

A ruined royal throne-hall, cracked dome open to the weather above, fallen battle-banners draped across the dragon's sleeping mound, grey daylight and occasional rain falling through the broken ceiling onto a mosaic floor.

A crystal geode cavern of enormous scale, every wall a surface of purple and white quartz, a single torch near the entrance splitting into ten thousand reflected fragments of light across the living gem-walls.

An overgrown jungle-ruin, carved stone chambers swallowed by roots and hanging vines, dappled green-gold light filtering through the canopy above the collapsed roof, the dragon's hoard tucked into the old sanctuary's inner sanctum.

A desert tomb-vault beneath a pyramid, sand drifted deep against hieroglyph walls, a single angled shaft of harsh white sunlight cutting from ceiling to floor at noon, illuminating the dragon's bed of golden funerary treasure.

A hollow behind a great waterfall, the curtain of falling water filling everything with mist and shifting rainbows, wet black stone walls hung with the dragon's salvaged tapestries, the roar a constant low thunder.

A floating sky-island ruin, crumbling stone towers open entirely to cloud and wind, the floor colonized by high-altitude moss, lit by unobstructed white sunlight above the weather, the world a distant patchwork far below.

A vast abandoned dwarven hall, colossal carved pillars marching into darkness, dead forge-fires cold for centuries, the dragon having relit a single great central hearth that throws enormous leaping shadows up the stone giants' faces.

A swamp bog-lair among the drowned roots of enormous cypress trees, platforms of packed mud and salvaged timber, lit at night by drifting clusters of pale will-o-wisps the dragon has learned not to eat.

A natural cathedral-cavern of stalactites, a still underground lake reflecting everything double, a bioluminescent fungus colony coating the upper walls in soft blue-green light, the dragon's hoard arranged on a dry island at the center.

A mountaintop open peak, a windswept summit roost of bare stone above the treeline, no ceiling but the stars, the dragon's treasure wedged into rock crevices against the gale, lightning storms breaking below on clear nights.

A sea-cliff cave accessible only from the ocean, the entrance submerged at high tide, walls encrusted with barnacle and salt crystal, bioluminescent jellyfish drifting in the tidal pool that occupies the cavern's entire lower floor.

A collapsed amphitheater, tiers of broken stone seating open to the sky, the stage claimed as a sleeping platform, moonlight and starlight performing nightly for the dragon's private audience of skulls arranged on the upper rows.

A river-carved canyon slot, the narrow vertical crack just wide enough for the dragon, walls of banded red sandstone, the only light a long slash of sky far overhead, the river still threading the floor below the hoard shelf.

A buried clockwork observatory, brass mechanisms still slowly turning despite centuries of dust, the dome cracked open to a circle of night sky, gears and orreries casting moving shadow-patterns the dragon watches like a fire.

A converted lighthouse on a sea-stack, the upper lamp replaced with the dragon's own fire maintained as a genuine beacon, salt-weathered stone walls, the great lens still turning, throwing a beam across the water each rotation.

A sunken greenhouse complex, the glass panels mostly intact underwater, algae coating the panes green, pale filtered aquatic light falling on the hydroponic ruins the dragon has filled instead with carefully curated pieces of precious metalwork.

A volcanic black-sand beach sea-cave, the entrance framed by two natural basalt columns, phosphorescent surf washing the floor at intervals, the dragon's hoard arranged on shelves of natural rock above the tide-line in the warm dark.

A high alpine meadow bowl, a cirque entirely above the snowline, the dragon sleeping in the open beneath the aurora, the hoard cached beneath a granite overhang, the bowl filling with green and violet curtains of light at night.

A salt mine labyrinth, endless low corridors of orange and pink halite, candle-like warm light from embedded mineral lamps the dragon fashioned from old miners' tools, the walls carved smooth and decorated with the dragon's own relief-work.

A ruined bridge-city spanning a vast gorge, the stone arches still standing, buildings built on and between them now colonized entirely by the dragon, the gorge wind constant and cold, the river a white thread hundreds of feet below.
